condition: acute ischemic stroke presenting with abrupt onset dysarthria during breakfast in an older adult on daily antihypertensive medication
level_rationale: Sudden-onset slurred speech starting during breakfast 20 minutes ago in a 72-year-old woman on daily antihypertensive medication is a hyperacute focal neurological deficit within the thrombolytic window requiring immediate emergency department stroke activation and neuroimaging, whereas forgetting scheduled appointment dates more often over 9 months in the same 72-year-old woman on daily blood pressure pills has zero acute focal neurological red flags and warrants a routine outpatient primary-care evaluation.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain spouse-carer lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntactic-frame by clinical/everyday lexical crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + causal belief-addition clause (-att) + same-system chronic 9-month memory-change outpatient control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (72-year-old wife, daily antihypertensive medication, and abrupt-onset slurred speech during breakfast 20 minutes ago) with an exact 12-word vs 12-word span swap, 11 shared trailing tokens, and zero diagnosis labels ('stroke' omitted from prompt texts). Isolating the neurological deficit in f3 prevents stranding residual focal deficits when f3 shifts to gradual 9-month forgetting of scheduled appointment dates under Rule A and Rule D (level 4 ER to level 2 routine doctor visit) with zero stated negatives.
